video_title: He's Made Money On 95% Of His Deals (Here's How)
gist: Cass Investments CIO Christopher Zuk (co-author with Tony Robbins of The Holy Grail of Investing) explains how his 13 billion dollar firm combines a few uncorrelated, moat-backed themes (Bitcoin infrastructure, GP stakes, pro sports, neoprime defense, energy) with percentage-based sizing to remove emotion.

insights.claim: Zuk's core rule is that diversification is the only free lunch: hold conviction positions but sized so you can endure being wrong or early, since concentrated investors get shaken out at the first drawdown in public markets and overconcentration plus leverage is a fast way to be wiped out.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Position sizing and staying power matter more than picking the single best idea.

insights.claim: Holding all seven Magnificent 7 stocks is not diversification because they are essentially the same trade that rises and falls together; true diversification is assets whose returns move independently, such as professional sports, GP stakes, and private assets.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Many retail portfolios are concentrated in one risk-on factor and less diversified than they look.

insights.claim: Citing Dalio's Holy Grail and Markowitz, Zuk says 8 to 15 uncorrelated assets can cut risk by about 80% and raise returns, but finding uncorrelated assets is hard because markets are so indexed that money flows into or out of the same risk-on/risk-off trade.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Explains the premium on genuinely non-correlated private and alternative exposures.
insights.quote: It's just 8 to 15 uncorrelated assets can reduce your risk by 80% and increase your return.

insights.claim: Investors should size positions by percentage of portfolio, not by dollar amount, because fixed-dollar sizing is emotional; a client worth about 800 million invested a fixed one million each time, until moved to 1 to 5 percent sizing.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Percentage sizing makes returns mechanical and removes anchoring on absolute dollars.

insights.claim: Cass uses a core-and-satellite structure: a durable, predictable non-market-correlated core, with satellite positions of about 50 basis points in venture-style names like Figure AI, Anthropic and SpaceX that can move the portfolio if they return 10x to 20x.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Small satellite bets give convex upside without threatening the core.

insights.claim: Cass claims it has made money on 95 percent of realized and unrealized private-market investments over 25 years, attributing it to removing emotion and always starting with the worst case, on the view that if you can live with it the upside takes care of itself.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Self-reported batting average; stress-test-first process is the claimed edge.
insights.quote: We literally on 95% of all of our realized and unrealized investments in the private markets, we've made money.

themes.theme: Theme plus moat: sports, GP stakes, Bitcoin

insights.claim: Cass sees Bitcoin, GP stakes and pro sports teams as sharing scarcity or a moat, chosen as macro themes first rather than because they are cool, and it says the three do not correlate with each other.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Framework: theme with a moat, then the best risk-adjusted vehicle.

insights.claim: The sports theme is cord cutting: as viewers move to streaming, live sports become the main way advertisers reach audiences; owning an NFL team is a league-protected monopoly with a 1/32nd share, paying about 450 million dollars in league revenue per team this year before any game is played.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Reason sports franchise valuations are supported by media economics, not trophy value.

insights.claim: GP stakes give exposure to the growth of private assets: Zuk expects opening 401(k) and 403(b) plans to private investments could send about a trillion dollars over a decade into private assets, and owning managers lets Cass earn the two-and-twenty instead of paying it.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Asset-manager fee streams are a way to play retirement-channel access to private markets.

insights.claim: The SEC rule change last June lets non-accredited investors buy private-company funds (SpaceX, Anthropic, OpenAI, Dodgers, PSG) with a 2,500 dollar minimum and quarterly liquidity; Zuk argues Buffett's real engine was private businesses whose value was not repriced daily.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Retail access to private markets is widening, creating fund-flow demand for late-stage names.

themes.theme: Picks-and-shovels approach to crypto and energy

insights.claim: Cass invests in crypto via infrastructure rather than tokens (picks and shovels), including early backing of firms that helped start Solana, because picking winning coins was too volatile and infrastructure offers more certainty; Zuk says he trades crypto but is an investor in the ecosystem, not the coins.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Infrastructure exposure gives crypto beta with less token-selection risk.

insights.claim: Zuk expects oil to go a lot higher because the supply-demand picture in energy is out of whack with underproduction versus demand growth, and Cass is buying energy businesses at about four times cash flow while also investing in small modular nuclear, storage and batteries.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Contrarian value in fossil energy amid ESG-driven capital flight; low entry multiples.

insights.claim: Zuk describes neoprimes such as Anduril, funded to self-develop products and sell them faster and cheaper, versus legacy primes on cost-plus contracts with no incentive for speed; a new chapter on space and defense was added to the paperback because the sector reached scale.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Business-model shift in defense procurement favors venture-backed neoprimes.

insights.claim: Allies agreeing to raise defense spending from about 2 percent to 5 percent of GDP is described as multiple trillions of dollars over decades by mandate, and Cass was an early investor in Saronic (spelled Seronic in the transcript), whose autonomous boat is credited with rescuing two pilots in the Strait of Hormuz this spring.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Structural European and allied defense demand supports autonomous defense-tech names.
insights.quote: our allies have agreed to increase their spending from roughly 2% of their gross domestic product to 5%

insights.claim: Cost asymmetry of drones drives defense change: you cannot use a million-dollar Tomahawk against a 30,000 dollar drone (Ferraris to shoot down Frisbees), so AI-driven cheap defenses are required; SpaceX now does work NASA once did.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Cheap-interceptor and autonomy vendors benefit from the cost-exchange problem.

themes.theme: Macro worries and AI labor impact

insights.claim: Zuk's main AI worry is jobs rather than Terminator scenarios: he expects no truck drivers within a decade, more robots in factory roles, and slower hiring as companies grow with fewer people, citing Figure AI robots making BMWs and sorting packages in UPS facilities.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Labor-substitution pressure in rote roles; service and relationship jobs retain value.

insights.claim: Zuk argues emotion and complexity are the enemies of execution, and cites cash and career risk as the reasons most professionals invest, cash burning a hole in the pocket or fear of being fired.
insights.speaker: guest Christopher Zuk, founder/chairman/CIO, Cass Investments
insights.so_what: Behavioral edge: separate emotion from decisions rather than react to doom headlines.
